title: Project Root & Monorepo Structure
description: Start at the root package.json to understand the monorepo layout. Pāvati Pustak is a Turborepo-based monorepo with three workspaces: apps/api (Express backend), apps/web (React SPA), and two internal packages (shared types and receipt engine). The root defines scripts for dev, build, and deploy across all packages.
languageLesson: Monorepo tooling: Turborepo orchestrates builds across TypeScript workspaces. The root package.json uses workspaces + turbo.json to parallelize type-checking and builds. SQL lives in Prisma migrations; Prisma schema is the source of truth for the database.

title: API Server Bootstrap
description: The Express server entry point at apps/api/src/index.ts is the highest fan-out file in the codebase (19 outbound edges). It mounts all route modules (auth, trusts, donations, receipts, campaigns, members, templates, reports, etc.), applies middleware (CORS, rate limiting, error handling), and wires up providers (storage, messaging). This is the single orchestration point for the entire backend.
languageLesson: Express server pattern: a single index.ts imports and mounts ~12 route modules plus middleware. Each module is a separate routes.ts file. The server uses http.ts as a thin Express wrapper and logger.ts for structured logging.

title: Database Schema (18 Models)
description: The Prisma schema defines the entire data model: Trust, User, Member, Donation, DonationSplit, Receipt, ReceiptTemplate, Campaign, Announcement, Notification, AuditLog, and more. Key relationships: a Trust has many Members and Donations; Donations have payment splits (cash/UPI); Receipts are generated per-donation with per-trust numbering. Six migration files show the schema evolution from init through QR codes, donation splits, and receipt uniqueness.
languageLesson: Prisma schema syntax: @id @default(autoincrement()), relations via @relation(), enums for roles and statuses. Migrations are timestamped SQL files; the migration_lock.toml pins the database provider.

title: Shared Package — Types, Schemas & Permissions
description: The packages/shared workspace is imported by both the API and web app, making it the contract layer. It exports TypeScript types (User, Trust, Donation, Receipt, Campaign), Zod validation schemas for all API inputs, permission constants organized by role (trust_admin, member, treasurer, etc.), and utility constants (festival lists, payment modes). The permissions module defines RBAC as a flat permission set; schemas use Zod for runtime validation.
languageLesson: Zod schemas: z.object({ name: z.string().min(1) }) for input validation. Permission model: flat permission strings like 'donation:create', 'trust:admin' checked by middleware. Shared package pattern: re-export everything from index.ts.

title: API Middleware — Auth, RBAC & Validation
description: Three middleware files form the security backbone. auth.ts extracts and verifies JWT tokens, attaching the user to the request. rbac.ts checks the user's role/permissions against required permission strings from the shared package. validate.ts applies Zod schemas to request bodies. rateLimit.ts provides request throttling. error.ts is the global error handler. These are imported by the server entry and used by every route module.
languageLesson: Middleware chain pattern: Express middleware functions (req, res, next) are composed. Auth middleware decodes JWTs; RBAC middleware checks permission sets; validate middleware parses request bodies against Zod schemas and returns 400 on failure.

title: API Route Modules
description: The API is organized into 12 route modules under apps/api/src/modules/. Each module (auth, trusts, donations, receipts, campaigns, members, templates, reports, announcements, notifications, uploads, dashboard, users) is a single routes.ts file exporting an Express Router. The server entry mounts them at path prefixes like /api/auth, /api/trusts, /api/donations. The donations module has the most outbound dependencies, coordinating with the shared schemas and middleware.
languageLesson: Express Router pattern: const router = Router(); router.post('/', authMiddleware, rbacMiddleware, validate(schema), handler); module.exports = router. Each module is self-contained with its own route handlers.

title: API Services — Receipts, Audit & Notifications
description: Services layer sits above routes. receipts.ts orchestrates PDF receipt generation by calling the receipt-engine package, persisting receipt records, and managing per-trust sequential numbering. audit.ts records all mutating actions to the AuditLog model. notifications.ts handles sending receipt notifications via WhatsApp/email channels. These services are called by route handlers and represent the business logic layer.
languageLesson: Service pattern: services encapsulate business logic separate from HTTP concerns. The receipt service coordinates: validate input → call receipt-engine for PDF → save receipt record → trigger notification. Audit logging is cross-cutting, called after mutations.

title: Receipt Engine — PDF Generation Package
description: packages/receipt-engine is a standalone package for generating receipt PDFs. It uses canvas-based rendering (node-canvas) to draw receipt templates with dynamic fields (donor name, amount, date, trust info), supporting background images and custom field layouts. pdf.ts is the main generator; layout.ts handles field positioning with pixel-level precision; types.ts defines the receipt template data model. The web app also uses this package for live preview rendering.
languageLesson: Canvas rendering: createCanvas() → ctx.fillText() for text, ctx.drawImage() for backgrounds. The receipt engine is isomorphic — same code runs server-side (PDF generation) and client-side (preview via HTML Canvas). TypeScript types define the contract between template editors and the renderer.

title: Web SPA Entry & Router
description: The React app boots at main.tsx, which sets up React 18 with StrictMode, renders the App component, and mounts to the DOM. The router (router.tsx) defines the full route tree with React Router v6: public routes (landing, donate, verify), auth routes (login, signup, forgot/reset password), and protected authenticated routes wrapped in the AppLayout. The layout component provides the sidebar navigation, trust switcher, and header.
languageLesson: React SPA architecture: main.tsx → <App /> → <BrowserRouter> → <Routes>. Protected routes use an auth guard that checks session state. The layout component wraps authenticated pages with navigation. React Router v6 uses element={<Component />} syntax.

title: Web API Client & Auth Store
description: The API client (api.ts) is the second most connected file (fan-in 33, fan-out 11). It wraps fetch() calls to every API endpoint with automatic token injection, trust context headers, and response parsing. The auth store (stores/auth.ts) manages client-side session state (user, trust, tokens) using a simple pub/sub pattern. auth-actions.ts coordinates login/logout/signup flows by calling the API client and updating the store. Every feature page imports api.ts for data fetching.
languageLesson: API client pattern: a centralized fetch wrapper that attaches Authorization headers, handles 401 redirects, and manages trust context. The auth store is a lightweight state manager — setSession() updates subscribers. No Redux/Zustand — custom pub/sub keeps the bundle small.

title: Web Shared Components & Layout
description: The UI component library (ui.tsx) provides Button, Card, Input, Select, Modal, Spinner, EmptyState, StatCard, PageHeader, and Pagination with branded maroon/cream theming. layout.tsx is the authenticated app shell: a permission-filtered sidebar navigation, trust switcher dropdown, responsive mobile menu, and header. utils.ts (highest fan-in at 36 dependents) provides shared helpers. Every feature page imports layout.tsx and ui.tsx.
languageLesson: Component design: ui.tsx exports ~12 reusable primitives with Tailwind CSS classes. layout.tsx defines navItems filtered by user permissions. utils.ts contains formatters, class mergers (cn/clsx pattern), and helper functions. CSS lives in apps/web/src/styles/index.css.

title: Donation Flow — End to End
description: The donation flow spans the full stack. CreateDonationPage.tsx (admin) records offline donations with split payment methods, proof uploads, and QR-based UPI collection. DonationsPage.tsx lists all donations with search/filter. DonatePage.tsx and MemberDonatePage.tsx handle public/member donations via campaign links. On the API side, donations/routes.ts processes the request, and receipts.ts generates the PDF receipt. This is the core business flow of the application.
languageLesson: Split payment model: a single donation can have multiple DonationSplit records (cash + UPI). Each split has its own verification status. The receipt is generated after all splits are recorded. QR codes are campaign-specific and show the trust's UPI ID.

title: Receipt & Template System
description: Receipts are PDF documents generated from customizable templates. ReceiptsPage.tsx lists receipts with send/download actions. ReceiptPreviewPage.tsx shows a live canvas preview. TemplateEditorPage.tsx provides a drag-and-drop editor for positioning text fields over a background image. ReceiptVerifyPage.tsx is a public page for verifying receipt authenticity. On the API, receipts/routes.ts handles CRUD and PDF generation by calling the receipt service.
languageLesson: Template system: each Trust has ReceiptTemplates with positioned fields (x, y, width, height). The editor uses pointer events for drag/resize. The receipt engine renders the template with live data. Public verification uses a unique receipt URL.

title: Deployment & Configuration
description: The Procfile at root defines the Heroku deployment: web process runs the API server, and the buildpack handles Prisma migration + build. Six migration files show the schema evolution. The project uses Vite for the web build, TypeScript with project references, and environment-based configuration. The seed file (prisma/seed.ts) populates initial data using shared constants.
languageLesson: Deployment pattern: Heroku Procfile runs 'node dist/index.js'. Prisma migrations run automatically via build script. Vite builds the SPA to static files served by the API. Config uses environment variables with typed defaults in config/index.ts.
